about: Sign-offs for the release gate (edakit gate). Each one counts only for the hash of its scope: 'circuit' = state_sha256 (graph, parts database, simulation config), 'layout' = layout_sha256 (layout files, artwork, footprint geometry), 'fab' = fab_sha256 (what the manufacturer builds from a gate run: Gerber layers, drill hits, BOM and CPL rows). When something there changes, it no longer counts – copy the new hash from the protocol header after the check was repeated. phase: 'export' blocks the release, 'order' and 'acceptance' come after the export. An accepted warning with scope 'decision' counts regardless of the hash and refers to a numbered decision in the docs. Parts are signed in their parts entry (field 'verified').

manual.text: Critical parts (U1 Nano pinout, C1 polarity, the LEDs, J1 servo pinout) checked a second time independently against datasheet and footprint – e.g. by the agent electrical-reviewer
manual.note: M-1: OK for state 861f9237…; requirements met: R-7, R-12. Second check on 2026-11-01 (edakit bc44fa7, offline gate 20261101-001257). U1's 30 pads match Arduino's Nano pinout by position (rows 15.24 mm; pad 15 = D12 and 16 = D13 at the USB end; 27 = 5V; 4/29 = GND); the pins match buttons.ino: D2–D6 LEDs, D8 servo, U1.14 = D11 start, U1.15 = D12 reset. C1 C439782: pad 1 with '+' on +5V, lead Ø0.6 mm (datasheet p. 6). LEDs XL-504SURD/UYD/UGD: flat and '+' agree with datasheet p. 7 (long lead = anode), every cathode on GND. J1: 1 GND / 2 +5V / 3 SERVO, pin 0.64 mm. R-7: a stalled servo draws 0.81 A for at most about 5.8 s – about 0.36 W in the MBR0520, its junction well below 125 °C; the polyfuse can at most trip. Notes (no block): C1's inrush on plug-in (~9 A for ~0.5 ms, 0.022 A²s against the MBR0520's 0.126 A²s); repeated 'ring now' with a jammed bell exceeds R-7's 6 s; open items in parts entries this check closes; main lacks the variants' HINT accepts – all for the next circuit change.

manual.text: Layout reviewed independently (manufacturability; mechanics: the Nano's USB at the edge; operation of the buttons; looks of the LED row) on the manufacturing files of a gate run – e.g. by the agent pcb-reviewer
manual.note: M-5: OK for fab hash a9b42ee5… (gate run 20261101-004618, edakit bc44fa7). Against the reviewed f314419f… (release 20261030-232729), edakit fab diff shows only the new order.json; every Gerber layer, the drills, BOM and CPL are equal, and the board never had an order-number placeholder. Order: JLCPCB, 2 layers, 1.6 mm, green/white, LeadFree HASL, Remove Mark, Economic PCBA top with the 2 × Ø1.152 mm tooling holes at (3.5, 45)/(81.5, 20), mask open and copper-free. Stage L warnings only D-21 (S1, S2, U1 print beyond the left edge, the 12 mm copper-free circle at (55, 25) on top). Notes for the next layout change: hand_solder_keep_mm 0.5 and [looks] as on esp32tht.

manual.text: Regulatory review: circuit and parts against EU law for the stated purpose (RoHS, REACH, radio, batteries, product safety) – the agent regulatory-reviewer in its own session; support, not legal advice: no claim to correctness, nothing legally guaranteed
manual.note: M-6: OK for state 1a518dc3… (electrical) and purpose private; requirements met: R-10. The board has no transmitter (the Nano's entry: compliance.radio none) and is powered only through the Nano's USB socket: VIN free, J1 a servo output, no battery, no mains, every net at most 5.5 V. RoHS, REACH, CE, WEEE and the battery rules do not apply to own use. Notes: the firmware detaches the servo 1 s after the rest move (the earlier note that it never does is obsolete); the jurisdiction is Austria – EMC in substance by EMVV 2015, at its end the bell goes to the municipal e-waste collection (D-36). Support, not legal advice: no claim to correctness, nothing legally guaranteed.

manual.text: At JLCPCB after the upload: assembly preview (buttons, resistors), BOM without missing parts, price
Acceptance of every delivered board: visual check, Nano plugged in, current through USB, every LED, both buttons, the servo swings
